---
title: GitHub Backups
---

GitHub jobs incrementally maintain complete Git mirrors and optionally collect
Git LFS objects, wikis, repository metadata, and release assets. Use
`github-repository` for an explicit URL list or `github-owner` to discover every
repository owned by an organization or user. Each job snapshots its combined
managed workspace to one or more configured restic repositories.

## Back up an explicit repository list

GitHub jobs use the shared `jobs` section and a GitHub-specific `source`:

```yaml
jobs:
  - job-id: example-github-repository
    type: github-repository
    description: Complete GitHub repository backup.
    restic-repository-ids:
      - personal-b2
      - personal-local
    tag: example-github-repository
    source:
      repository-urls:
        - git@github.com:example/example-repository.git
        - git@github.com:example/another-repository.git
      authentication:
        git:
          ssh:
            private-key:
              file: /var/run/secrets/github/ssh-private-key
            known-hosts:
              file: /var/run/secrets/github/known-hosts
        api:
          token:
            env: GITHUB_MIGRATION_TOKEN
      components:
        git: true
        lfs: true
        wiki: true
        metadata: true
        release-assets: true
      migration-timeout-seconds: 3600
```

Every component flag is required, and at least one must be `true`. `lfs`
requires `git`. Every URL uses the same component and authentication settings.
The optional restic `tag` still defaults to `job-id`.

Only `github.com` clone URLs are accepted:

```text
git@github.com:OWNER/REPOSITORY.git
https://github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY.git
```

Credentials, query strings, and fragments embedded in the URL are rejected.
The URL list must be non-empty and identify distinct repositories; SSH and
HTTPS URLs for the same repository cannot appear together. The previous
singular `repository-url` field is accepted temporarily for migration.

## Discover an organization or user

Use `type: github-owner` to discover repositories instead of maintaining the
URL list manually:

```yaml
jobs:
  - job-id: example-organization
    type: github-owner
    restic-repository-ids:
      - personal-local
    source:
      owner-url: https://github.com/example
      clone-protocol: ssh
      components:
        git: true
        lfs: false
        wiki: false
        metadata: false
        release-assets: false
      migration-timeout-seconds: 3600
```

The owner may be an organization or a user. Enumeration includes every public,
private, archived, and fork repository visible to the active GitHub credentials
and owned by that account. `clone-protocol` defaults to `ssh`; choose `https`
when using HTTPS Git authentication. With no `authentication.api.token`,
enumeration uses the current credentials from `gh auth login`. Containers and
scheduled jobs can provide the token from an environment variable or mounted
file. Cloning continues to use the separately configured Git credentials or SSH
agent.

The repository list is refreshed on every run. Newly discovered repositories
get new owner/repository workspaces. Repositories no longer returned by GitHub
are omitted from new snapshots but retained in older immutable snapshots; their
unused local workspace is not deleted automatically.

Owner-job dry runs contact GitHub read-only to show the precise discovered plan.
They do not create local files, run Git, or contact Restic.

## Credentials

On an interactive laptop, the simplest configuration omits `authentication`.
GitHub API commands then use the current `gh auth login` session, while clone
operations use the normal Git credential helper or SSH agent and configuration.
Configure the explicit secret sources below only when those credentials are not
available, such as in a container or Kubernetes CronJob.

Every configured secret source contains exactly one `env` or `file` key. The
environment variable or file is read again on every run, which works with
rotated Kubernetes Secrets and other secret managers. Secret values are never
placed in command arguments, logs, manifests, or the audit log.

For SSH clone URLs, omit `authentication.git` to use the existing SSH agent and
configuration, or configure both a private key and `known_hosts`. Configured
keys are copied to temporary owner-only files, and strict host verification is
always enabled. Generate a pinned host entry according to GitHub's
[SSH host key guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/githubs-ssh-key-fingerprints).

For HTTPS clone URLs, use a token without putting it in the URL:

```yaml
authentication:
  git:
    https:
      token:
        env: GITHUB_GIT_TOKEN
```

The CLI supplies it through a temporary Git askpass helper. When this source is
omitted, Git uses its existing credential configuration; public repositories
need no authentication.

When `authentication.api.token` is omitted, API-backed components use the
current credentials from `gh auth login`. Containers and scheduled jobs without
that login should configure a token from an environment variable or mounted
file. GitHub's migration API currently requires a compatible **classic personal
access token** and repository-owner access; fine-grained tokens and GitHub App
tokens are not supported for this API. The default OAuth token created by
`gh auth login` may therefore receive HTTP 403 even when it has `repo` and
`admin:org` scopes. To keep using the local `gh` credential store, authenticate
it with a compatible classic PAT through `gh auth login --with-token`. See
GitHub's [organization migration API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/migrations/orgs)
and [user migration API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/migrations/users).

For a Kubernetes CronJob, mount files or inject environment variables from a
Secret and point the job at their names—do not put secret values in YAML:

```yaml
env:
  - name: GITHUB_MIGRATION_TOKEN
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: github-backup
        key: api-token
volumeMounts:
  - name: github-ssh
    mountPath: /var/run/secrets/github
    readOnly: true
```

The container needs `git`, `git-lfs` when LFS is enabled, `gh` when API-backed
components are enabled, and `restic`. `make install-deps` installs these tools
with Homebrew for local use.

## Components

| Component | Backed-up data | Update behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `git` | Every object reachable through remote Git refs, including complete branch and tag history | Initial `git clone --mirror`; later `git remote update --prune` |
| `lfs` | All Git LFS objects reachable from the mirror | `git lfs fetch --all origin` |
| `wiki` | The repository wiki as a separate Git mirror | Missing or empty wikis are recorded as `not-present` |
| `metadata` | GitHub's official migration export, including issues, pull requests, comments, attachments, and release metadata | A new migration archive is requested and downloaded each run |
| `release-assets` | Binary files attached to releases | Missing or changed assets download atomically; remotely deleted assets are removed only after a complete successful update |

A Git-only job sets `git: true` and every other component to `false`. It needs
only Git authentication and never invokes `gh` for an explicit repository-list
job. Git history contains commits, branches, tags, trees, and normal Git file
content. It does **not** contain issue discussions, pull-request comments,
submodule repository contents, or commits already deleted from every remote ref.
Without `lfs`, it contains LFS pointer files but not the referenced large
objects. An owner job still invokes `gh` to discover its repository list.

## Run and inspect

Use the described arrow-key TUI or explicit commands:

```sh
uv run restic-backups job list
uv run restic-backups job run example-github-repository \
  --repository personal-b2 --repository personal-local
uv run restic-backups job status
uv run restic-backups job status example-github-repository
uv run restic-backups github-repository data-dir example-github-repository
uv run restic-backups generic snapshot list example-github-repository \
  --repository personal-b2
uv run restic-backups generic restic run --backup example-github-repository \
  --repository personal-b2 ls latest --tag example-github-repository
```

With no job ID, `job status` shows one row for every job and destination,
including the latest snapshot ID and time, the local export time, and component
states. Snapshots are matched using each job's configured tag, which defaults to
its job ID. Each destination repository is queried only once, even when many
jobs share it. Passing a job ID limits the snapshot table and adds that job's
detailed component errors.

The status table reads restic snapshot metadata, not backed-up file contents.
It can contact remote storage when the required metadata is not already cached.

GitHub jobs are also selectable from **Snapshots** and **Advanced restic**.
Use `restic ls` to browse files in a snapshot. The different `restic list`
command lists internal repository objects and requires an object type such as
`packs`, `snapshots`, or `keys`; it does not list configured backup jobs.

The TUI preselects a sole enabled destination. With several destinations, all
start unchecked and must be selected with Space. An explicit-list dry run
validates the plan without calling Git, GitHub, or restic and without writing
the workspace. An owner dry run first contacts GitHub read-only to discover the
exact repository list, but it likewise never runs Git, contacts restic, or
writes the workspace:

```sh
uv run restic-backups job run example-github-repository \
  --repository personal-b2 --dry-run
```

## Managed workspace and snapshots

The reusable local workspace lives beside the selected config:

```text
data/github-repositories/<job-id>/
  backup-manifest.json
  <owner>/<repository>/
    repository.git/
    wiki.git/
    github-export/
    release-assets/
```

The manifest records every source, the update time, and a safe status for every
repository component: `updated`, `unchanged`, `stale`, `not-present`, `failed`, or
`disabled`. If one component fails, the workflow still attempts the others and
all selected destinations. Existing local component data is included as
`stale`; the command creates the best available snapshot and exits nonzero when
anything failed. Disabled cached components are not included.

Before updating source data, the workflow checks that every selected restic
repository exists and, when metadata is enabled, that the active GitHub
credentials can read the migration endpoint. A job-wide path or authorization
error therefore stops before repositories are fetched. Repository-specific
component errors encountered after those checks still use the best-available
snapshot behavior above.

Restic splits input into content-defined chunks and deduplicates identical
chunks **within each restic repository**. Stable Git pack files, LFS objects,
migration files, and release assets therefore do not need to be uploaded again.
The workflow disables automatic Git maintenance and repacking because repacking
can rewrite otherwise unchanged Git objects and reduce deduplication. Separate
restic repositories do not share chunks, so two destinations each store their
own copy. See restic's [repository design](https://restic.readthedocs.io/en/stable/100_references.html#repository-design).

Restore a snapshot with the normal restic command, then clone the restored bare
repository into a working tree:

```sh
uv run restic-backups generic restic run --backup example-github-repository \
  restore latest --target /tmp/github-restore
git clone "$(find /tmp/github-restore -type d \
  -path '*/example/example-repository/repository.git' -print -quit)" \
  restored-repository
```

### Recovery expectations

| Component | Recovery path | Limitation |
|---|---|---|
| `git` | Push the restored mirror to an empty repository | GitHub-managed refs may be rejected; branches and tags can be pushed separately |
| `lfs` | Run `git lfs push --all` from the restored mirror | Available only when LFS was enabled for the backup |
| `metadata` | Retain the extracted GitHub migration export for migration or manual recovery | No direct, self-service import back into GitHub.com |

GitHub documents its migration archive as an export for moving repositories
from GitHub.com to GitHub Enterprise Server. Imports cannot be started through
the public REST API. See GitHub's
[organization migration API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/migrations/orgs)
and
[GitHub.com export guide](https://docs.github.com/en/migrations/using-ghe-migrator/exporting-migration-data-from-githubcom).

`restic-backups` stores the extracted migration contents and does not currently
provide a metadata import command. Treat metadata snapshots as archival and
disaster-recovery material rather than a guaranteed round trip into GitHub.com.
Restoring metadata to GitHub.com may require GitHub-supported migration help or
custom API recreation, which may not preserve original IDs, timestamps,
authorship, or every relationship.

## Deliberate limits

This workflow does not export GitHub Actions artifacts, logs or caches,
packages, secret values, forks as independent repositories, automatically
discovered submodule repositories, or GitHub Enterprise. Add each independent
Git or submodule repository URL that must be retained.
